claims.text: The untreated 316L stainless steel substrate has a native coarse-grained microstructure.
The untreated 316L substrate has a typical native surface oxide layer.
Electro spark deposition of mechanically alloyed CoCrFeNiMo0.85 powder will form a thin HEA coating on 316L stainless steel.
A surface pre-treatment or interlayer will improve adhesion of the HEA coating to 316L.
The deposited HEA coating will be dense and fine-grained.
The deposited HEA coating will be well adhered to the substrate.
The HEA coating will rapidly form a passive surface oxide enriched in Mo and Cr.
The passive oxide film will act as a protective barrier.
Formation of the passive oxide film will refine the coating microstructure.
The passive-film barrier will enhance corrosion resistance.
The passive-film barrier will improve wear performance.
Improved interfacial adhesion will make the protective coating durable under operational stress.
The coated component will have significantly greater surface hardness than untreated 316L.
The coated component will have better wear resistance than untreated 316L.
The coated component will provide superior corrosion protection relative to untreated 316L.
The intervention should remain effective during exposure to 3.5 wt.% NaCl at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
A hardness improvement of at least 20%, together with reduced wear and corrosion rates, is an example of a successful outcome relative to the uncoated control.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator presents the fine-grained coating as existing before passive-film formation, while the mechanism says that the subsequently formed passive film refines the microstructure. This creates an inconsistent causal ordering.
